label: FP
reason: Both alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) targets the response output of 'filter'. Alert 2 (java/ldap-injection) targets the 'filter' variable assignment. In both cases, the sink value depends on 'bar' from doSomething. Analysis of doSomething (lines 108-113) reveals that 'valuesList.remove(0)' shifts the user parameter 'param' to index 0, causing 'valuesList.get(1)' to resolve to the constant string 'moresafe' instead of 'param'. Consequently, the sink value is not attacker-controlled.

evidence.note: doSomething logic: valuesList.remove(0) shifts param to index 0, so get(1) returns constant 'moresafe', not user input.
LDAP filter sink uses 'bar', which resolves to 'moresafe' (constant), not 'param'.
XSS sink prints 'filter', which contains 'bar' (constant 'moresafe'), not user input.
